description: Canonical source of truth for the BurnBar Data & Privacy Control Center. One entry per user-facing data domain. Codegen emits typed consts for web (TS), Apple (Swift), and Android (Kotlin) so the domain list + encryption tiers never drift from firestore.rules / docs/PRIVACY.md. A CI drift check (driftcheck.mjs) asserts every users/{uid}/ collection in firestore.rules is covered by some domain's firestorePaths or listed in `excludedCollections`.

encryptionTiers.server_readable: Stored as plaintext; BurnBar's servers can read it (operational metadata, telemetry, billing).
encryptionTiers.zero_access: Encrypted at rest; BurnBar cannot read the content but holds the wrapped key escrow path under user-controlled device trust.
encryptionTiers.end_to_end: Sealed on-device with the vault key; BurnBar never sees plaintext or the key. Deletion is genuine ciphertext deletion.

domains.title: Usage & Spend
domains.summary: Per-session token counts, cost estimates, and provider/model/device telemetry. Project names and budget labels are sealed on-device; the server groups spend only by opaque per-project hashes.

domains.title: Conversations & Chat
domains.summary: Assistant chats, CLI agent transcripts, mobile mission prompts/results, saved text snippets, rollback scope/diagnostics, approval rules, agent personas, subscription graph edges, and conversation recall metadata are sealed on-device before Firestore receives them.
deviceOnly: subscription graph edges and display text

domains.title: Searchable Session Logs
domains.summary: Full conversation bodies + the encrypted search index + project memory. Sealed on-device; the server holds only ciphertext, aggregate cockpit facets, and opaque search/integrity hashes. NOTE: the keyword search index is deterministic — repeated and co-occurring search terms produce stable keyed digests, so the server can learn which terms recur and appear together across your logs (the search structure), and the integrity hashes can confirm a guessed body or chunk; every title, snippet, body, and path stays sealed and unreadable.

domains.title: Pensieve Knowledge
domains.summary: Your private semantic memory: repo docs, notes, and chat-derived memories your agents recall. Cloaked vectors + sealed text; the server runs ANN over them without reading your content, though these structures still reveal some recurrence/co-occurrence patterns. NOTE: a connected repo stores only an opaque keyed match token plus a sealed repo name — the cleartext repo name is observed transiently server-side only to route an inbound GitHub push webhook, never stored.

domains.title: Provider Accounts
domains.summary: Connected AI provider accounts. Labels + status only — the actual credentials live in Google Cloud Secret Manager, never in your data tree.
deviceOnly: secret material (in Secret Manager, not the user tree)

domains.title: Connected Devices & Pairings
domains.summary: Your paired Macs, phones, and relays (Hermes, Pi agent, iroh) and which can talk to your account. NOTE: end-to-end relay frames AND the hosted chat gateway are both sealed and never readable by the server — the gateway routes ciphertext per-link and never reads message text, sender names, or attachment file names. The per-agent subscription graph is cloaked behind opaque keyed doc ids.
deviceOnly: end-to-end relay + gateway frame contents (message text, sender names, attachment file names — all sealed on-device)

domains.title: External Agent Access (MCP)
domains.summary: Coding agents you've granted hosted-MCP access to, the scopes they hold, and their access audit trail.
deviceOnly: decrypted search/recall results (decrypted only in the local shim)

domains.title: Agent Control & Escrow
domains.summary: Computer-use (Agent Control) sessions and their tamper-evident escrow audit trail.

domains.title: Media
domains.summary: Files, screen, and video relayed between your Mac and phones (Floo media). NOTE: an attachment manifest records only an opaque content hash, mime type, byte size, an opaque per-peer device-id hash, direction, and timestamps — the human-readable file name is sealed on-device (sealedFilename) and never readable by the server.

domains.title: Plan & Billing
domains.summary: Your subscription entitlements (Cloud Pro, Ultra) and their change history.

domains.title: Device Trust & Vault Keys
domains.summary: Which devices are trusted to decrypt your data, and the wrapped vault keys that make end-to-end encryption possible. The crux of the whole E2EE model.
deviceOnly: the vault key itself (Keychain / 0600 file, never uploaded)

domains.title: Access Audit Timeline
domains.summary: A unified, tamper-evident log of who/what accessed your data, when — across every device, agent, and grant.

excludedCollections.budgetRules: Local automation rules; surfaced in Budgeting UI, not a privacy data domain.
excludedCollections.high_risk_action_nonces: Server-issued single-use nonces gating high-risk actions; ephemeral throttle/anti-replay state, not user content.
excludedCollections.cloud_profile: Account profile basics (shown in Account settings).
